newsitem.title: UK: EUROPEAN SHARES RISE HESITANTLY AFTER WALL ST SURGE.
newsitem.headline: EUROPEAN SHARES RISE HESITANTLY AFTER WALL ST SURGE.

text.p: European share markets dutifully rose on Wednesday after Wall Street came close to recording its biggest points gain ever, but investors were more wary than their American counterparts.

The dollar had a quiet morning after data on Tuesday indicated that a U.S. interest rate rise was less likely, news that propelled the Dow Jones Industrial Average up 179.01 points to 6,962.03 overnight.
London stocks started the day enthusiastically, with the FTSE 100 index bursting through its intra-day record of 4,466.3, set on March 11, in pre-market trading.

But even then dealers were wary of any spectacular performance the day before British parliamentary elections which are expected to produce a Labour government, a great unknown as the party has been in opposition for 18 years.
"It's not the kind of thing you expect on the eve of a general election," said one equity salesman.

His caution proved correct, and by mid morning the FTSE had sunk to 4,444.8 points, albeit 11.6 points up on the day. However, this gain was a modest 0.26 percent compared with 2.64 percent rise on the Dow.

"People were not quite so happy to buy at that level," said a trader after the market slipped from the high. "There's the feeling too that Wall Street is very volatile at the moment and one day's big gain doesn't make a summer."
British gilts (government bonds) were firm but stayed wary before the general election on Thursday.
The Wall Street rally was triggered by weaker than expected wage inflation and durable goods orders on Tuesday.
The Dow rally fell short of a 187 point one-day rise after the "Black Monday" crash of October, 1987. But in percentage terms it was modest compared with the 10 percent gain on October 21, 1987.
Germany followed the Wall Street trend most faithfully among the leading European markets, with the DAX index being propelled up 65.23 points or 1.93 percent to 3,448.42.
This was close to its all-time high but dealers still reported scepticism about the Wall Street stength.

French shares were also firm but restrained with the CAC-40 index up 0.76 percent. But shares in chemical and pharmaceuticals group Rhone-Poulenc SA jumped 9.1 percent to 205 francs at the opening after the company reported a 6.5 percent rise in its first quarter net income.
Election worries also overshadowed Paris, with a poll showing the centre-right coalition government slightly ahead of the opposition Socialists.
On the foreign exchange market, the dollar drifted below 127 yen back to where it was at the European close on Tuesday but edged up against the mark.
The dollar was sensitive to a series of U.S. data due later in the day which are expected to give further clues about whether the U.S. Federal Reserve will raise rates.
These include first quarter gross domestic product due at 1230 GMT. It is forecast to rise by 4.1 percent after a 3.8 percent increase previously.
At 1400 GMT the market will see the Chicago Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) and the New York National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) data, both for April.
"If we see the data coming in softer than expected, dollar/mark will weaken," said Deborah Read, economic adviser at Bank America in London.
"Concerning dollar/yen, the drop will not be so pronounced, since the difference in the trends in the U.S. and Japanese economies is still quite wide," she said.
"It's a case of stronger numbers, stronger dollar more than anything else now," said Ian Amstad, economist at Bankers Trust in London.
The dollar was at 1.7266 marks at mid morning against 1.7235 in late European trade on Tuesday. It was at 126.75 yen, unchanged from late on Tuesday.
STOCKS AT 0900 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 11.6 points or 0.26 percent at 4,466.3.
The Paris CAC-40 index rose 19.78 points (0.76 percent) at 2,622.64.
Frankfurt's DAX index gained 65.23 points (1.93 percent) to 3,448.42.
